security_privacy_cost_impact: Tightens only. created_by at INSERT is now bound by a restrictive closure on all nineteen tables that grant it, so no permissive policy, however loose, can admit a row naming another creator; every client-insertable *_by column must carry its column's pinned closure; and every permissive policy on the 25 client-writable app tables is pinned by name, command, roles and exact deparse, so a widening -- a new sibling or an in-place edit -- fails migrate-clean by name. psqlLex also refuses a spelled change of client encoding and is tested at odd runs of 3 and 5. No data, secret or cost impact. The review round tightens further: no client role (anon, authenticated, PUBLIC) may hold TRUNCATE, TRIGGER, REFERENCES or MAINTAIN on any relation in app, private or public, any privilege on a view, materialized view or foreign table there (unless pinned and security_invoker; none pinned), or any privilege on a table in private or public (none pinned); the 33 member-scope narrowings are pinned by exact deparse and the five member_scope_* helpers by body; SET NAMES is refused anywhere in fed text.
migration_and_data_impact: ONE MIGRATION: 127_created_by_on_insert_is_caller.sql (nineteen restrictive INSERT policies and an apply-time block), numbered in MOD-120's 115-129 range by the Owner's answer of 2026-10-03. 091's block superseded by a final-state replacement; the 030, 040, 080, 081, 090, 100 and 120 replacements carry 127's closures. Declared in the snapshot's not-applied tail. It refuses nothing that works today: every permissive INSERT policy on the nineteen already required created_by = the caller.
compatibility_impact: Additive and forward. Cases 1058 -> 1077 (nineteen created_by-alone cases) -> 1078 (user-a-cannot-update-user-b-profile, review round); tests 675 -> 677; foundation-contract floors 72 -> 73 tests and 418 -> 464 -> 480 assertions, identity-isolation 304 -> 305 and 2152 -> 2166. Probes 16 -> 19 -> 21. Every later batch that adds, drops or rewrites a permissive policy on a client-writable app table must update PERMISSIVE_POLICIES in the same diff; one that rewrites a member-scope narrowing or a member_scope_* helper updates PINNED_POLICIES or POLICY_HELPER_FUNCTIONS; one that grants a client anything on a view or on a table in private or public pins it, with its reason.
known_limitations: A client-encoding change whose name or SET words are computed at run time (set_config('client_' || 'encoding', ...), EXECUTE of a SET built by concatenation in a DO body) is outside psqlLex's list; a byte rule would refuse 4,611 places in 77 of 86 fed files. A spelled SET NAMES is refused anywhere since the review round (C0 F6). Owed, for a reviewer.

The other roles' reach (app_worker, service_role, RFC-2026-023 command roles) is read by no rule here; schema public is closed for CLIENT privileges by the review round's client privilege probe. A client may still EXECUTE an invoker function created in public (it bypasses nothing).
Remedy (b), created_by out of the client INSERT grant, is not taken, by the Owner's answer of 2026-10-03.

Restrictive policies are not in the permissive probe.
